study_question: For 20 S1 taxa with reliable island-level historical loss reports in the Azores, how many can be identified in a separately compiled 2010/2016 island checklist, and on which other islands are they documented as present? Only coverage/current residual distribution, not past source rescue.

azores2016.source_origin_bibliography: Borges et al. 2010 terrestrial and marine biota

independent_data_limitation: Azores 2016 checklist partly draws on literature overlapping with historical S1 cases, so it is a separate source file but not fully independent field replication.

normalisation.name_primary: Unicode NFKC casefold trim collapse spaces; exact source scientificName matching only if unique source taxon key
normalisation.name_secondary: Latin binomial Genus epithet, only if unique SOURCE taxon rank species and unambiguous; never join variety/subspecies to species or interpret identical epithet as same genus
normalisation.name_sensitivity: Remove trailing numeric citation annotations only as a predeclared sensitivity. Do not call taxonomy synonym resolution.
normalisation.locality_rules: Only unique exactly matched canonical island after diacritic/space normalization, optional leading Azores/Açores and suffix Island, no expansion of 'Azores' or multiple island lists
normalisation.uncertain_occurrence_status: Missing/unknown/unrecognized and absent must not be treated as confirmed presence.
normalisation.missing_native_status: separately report unknown; do not imply native when empty

provenance_warning: 2016 checklist distribution often derives from circa 2010 book, and S1 last-record dates vary; it cannot be called pre-loss population structure for all cases.
2016 checklist present on a reported lost island is a data conflict requiring taxonomy/temporal audit, not proof of recolonization.
The checklist is not a complete 2016 survey with uniform effort; missing taxa/islands remain unknown, not verified absent.
Only one archipelago in this crosswalk; do not generalize same-species loss concentration across 4 archipelagos.
Do not condition any risk model on extirpations counted as predictors or use S2 historical loss outcomes as environmental covariates.
stop_conditions: Either original provider original-file SHA or byte count mismatch
Unexpected field terms/core and distribution tables
Missing or ambiguous taxon keys without unambiguous joins
Impossible exact raw 24/20 S1 Azores counts
Do not open S3/S4 Macaronesian native flora response sheets or any Structural 529-mammal/BioTIME/RLS protected responses
